input: Draft an author bio for my upcoming short story collection

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: An author bio can range from a single sentence to several paragraphs; knowing the expected length shapes everything about how much detail to include.
The bio is about the author, so knowing their actual background, credentials, and publishing history is essential raw material.
Where the bio will appear (back cover, publisher website, literary magazine, press kit) affects tone, format, and what to emphasise.
Author bios range from formal/literary to warm/conversational to quirky/playful; the desired tone must match the collection's voice and the author's personal brand.
Knowing what the author most wants the reader to take away — credibility, relatability, intrigue about the stories — steers which elements get foregrounded.
Publishers or submission guidelines often impose a strict word or character count; ignoring this could make the draft unusable.
Whether the bio should be written in first or third person is a concrete formatting decision that changes the entire draft.

gold.taskTitle: Draft author bio for short story collection
gold.taskDescription: Write a professional author biography to accompany the user's upcoming short story collection.

questions.title: What is the word or character limit for the bio?
questions.description: Establish whether a publisher, platform, or submission guideline imposes a specific length constraint on the bio.

questions.title: Where exactly will this bio appear?
questions.description: Identify the placement — back cover copy, publisher website, literary journal, press kit, etc. — so format and register can be matched accordingly.

questions.title: Should the bio be written in first or third person?
questions.description: Determine the grammatical person required, as this is a fundamental structural decision that changes the entire draft.

questions.title: What tone should the bio convey — formal, conversational, or playful?
questions.description: Establish the desired voice and register so the bio aligns with the collection's style and the author's personal brand.

questions.title: What writing credentials or publications should be highlighted?
questions.description: Gather the author's relevant background — prior publications, awards, MFA or other credentials, notable placements — to use as source material.

questions.title: What is the collection about, and what genre does it span?
questions.description: Understanding the themes, genre, and subject matter of the collection helps tailor the bio so it contextualises the author's voice and work.

questions.title: What impression should readers be left with after reading the bio?
questions.description: Clarify the primary goal — establishing literary credibility, creating personal connection, building curiosity about the stories — to prioritise the right elements.
